transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably nothing major at all. I just... I keep messing up little things here and there. Nothing terrible, I promise! Just silly mistakes that make me feel a bit foolish. 

Like, I'll write down the wrong time on a class sheet over at the senior center. Or I'll be tinkering with a project, and I'll measure a board once, but I still end up cutting it a hair short just because I kind of... skipped over the small print on the tape. It's a little embarrassing to even bring up, to be honest. I just thought I should see if it's something I need to worry about. Is that the sort of thing you help people with?
Have these kinds of mistakes been happening since childhood?

Oh, goodness... well, yes, I suppose they have. I hope that doesn't make me sound too terribly scatterbrained. 

I mean, even way back in elementary school, my teachers used to write notes on my report cards about it. They were always very kind—they'd usually start by saying I was a bright boy, which was nice of them to say. But... well, they'd also mention that I'd forget my books at home, or somehow lose my homework before I could turn it in. Just clumsy kid stuff, really. 

And I guess I had a bit of a habit of staring out the window... just sort of drifting off unless someone gently nudged me to stay on track. It wasn't that I was trying to be a bad student or ignore the lesson, I promise! I always wanted to do well. I just... lost my place sometimes. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for, Doctor.
When you were in school, did you have a lot of trouble with reading, writing, or math itself?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I actually did quite alright with the subjects themselves. I hope I didn't make it sound like I couldn't understand the work! 

Reading was fine, and math... well, I could do the math, I just... you know, I might copy the numbers down wrong from the board, or forget to carry a one. Just those silly little careless errors I mentioned before. But the actual concepts? I understood those just fine. I was a capable student, really I was, just... a bit prone to little slips. I hope that clears it up? I wouldn't want you to think I was struggling with the actual learning part.
Have these difficulties been getting noticeably worse over time?

Well, I wouldn't say they've gotten terribly worse in a scary way, if that makes sense. I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill. But... I suppose they have been a bit more noticeable lately. 

My wife and I downsized and moved into a condo about a year and a month ago, and... well, ever since then, it feels like these little slip-ups are just getting in the way a bit more. Maybe it's just the new environment, or trying to organize everything in a smaller space, but it's been a little frustrating. Not that I can't handle it, of course! It's just... I've definitely noticed it interfering a bit more since the move. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen when you change routines? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you often feel unusually restless or fidgety, or find it hard to sit still?

Oh, goodness, no, I wouldn't say I'm terribly fidgety in a disruptive way! I certainly know how to behave myself, I promise. I wouldn't want you to think I'm bouncing off the walls like a little boy or anything like that. 

But... well, I suppose if I'm sitting through a whole meeting, or even just having a quiet evening at the condo with my wife, I do sometimes get this... sort of ants-in-my-pants feeling? It's nothing major, really! I just suddenly want to get up, maybe check on something in the kitchen, or just putter around the living room for a bit. I always try to be quiet about it so I don't bother anyone. It's just a little urge to stretch the legs, I suppose. Is it alright if I just need to move around a little like that? I hope that doesn't make me sound too restless.
Do you have trouble keeping your attention on tasks, even ones you want to do?

Oh, well... no, not really. I mean, if it's something I want to do, I'm usually quite good at sticking with it. I hope I haven't given the impression that I just can't focus on anything at all! 

If I'm working on a puzzle or reading the paper, I can sit there and get it done. I suppose my mind might wander just a tiny bit if a task is terribly boring, but who doesn't experience that, right? I always make sure to finish what I start, eventually. I just want to reassure you that I'm not entirely scatterbrained. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to.
Did you have trouble learning a specific school subject, like reading, spelling, or math?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't want you to think I was a poor student or anything like that! School was quite a long time ago for me, obviously, but... well, I always managed just fine with reading and spelling. Math, too. 

I might not have been the absolute top of the class, but I certainly didn't have any terrible trouble learning them. I always made sure to put in the effort and do what the teachers asked of me. I hope it's alright that I don't have any big struggles to report there? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture, and I'd hate to make it sound like I couldn't keep up in school when I really did try my best. Is that the sort of answer you're looking for?
Did you ever have persistent trouble learning to read, spell, write, or do math at school?

Oh, I think we... we just touched on that, didn't we? I hope I didn't confuse things! But no, really, I didn't have any persistent trouble like that. I could read and write and do my sums just fine, I promise. 

I'd hate for you to think I was hiding some sort of learning problem from you, but I honestly got through all of that without any major hiccups. I always wanted to make my parents and teachers proud, you know? So I just put my head down and did the work. I hope it's okay that I don't have a different answer for you this time around! I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Before age 12, did you have these kinds of attention or restlessness problems in more than one setting, like both at school and at home?

Well, um... I suppose if we're going all the way back to elementary school... I mean, I was a good boy, I really was. I never caused any trouble or ran around the classroom or anything like that. I hope you know I always tried to be respectful.

But, well, I guess my teachers did sometimes write on my report cards that I was... you know, a bright boy, but maybe a bit forgetful? I'd accidentally leave a book at home, or... or misplace a homework assignment. Just silly little mistakes, really. And they might have mentioned that I had a habit of staring out the window if they weren't right there reminding me to look at the chalkboard. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult, I promise! I just... my mind would wander a bit, both at school and sometimes when my mother asked me to do chores at home. But I always meant well. I hope that doesn't sound too awful? I really don't want you to think I was a bad kid. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
